2028 Lexus TX 650 Packs the Premium Touch on Top of the Toyota Tundra, Only Across Imagination Land
15 photos
Photo: jlord8 / Instagram
Even in this day and age, when in some regions like North America the days of passenger cars feel numbered because everyone wants only crossovers, SUVs, and trucks, Lexus continues to offer a variety of models for everyone. Well, almost everyone, actually.
They used to have both coupe and convertible models in the roster, but now they rely solely on the compact Lexus IS executive sedan and the larger ES mid-sizer in the passenger car roster. The CUV area is well covered with the UX, NX, RZ, RX, TZ, and TX nameplates. There are also two legacy SUVs packing a tough body-on-frame construction – the mid-size GX and the full-size LX.
But do you know exactly what’s missing and America loves? Yep, trucks, that’s right. North America tried its hand at luxury pickups not long ago and came out suffering, so they didn’t use premium nameplates anymore and instead topped the regular models with premium trim levels that border on insanity in terms of creature comforts and pricing, like the Denali Ultimate from GMC.
Toyota Motor North America has its own equivalent – the 2027 Toyota Tundra Capstone, which starts from $83k sans destination and options! That’s pretty high, right? Alas, it turns out maybe a Lexus pickup truck isn’t a crazy thing. Well, it is, actually, specifically when it’s done for the 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, like the Meso Customs TX1, which started life as a CGI project done by a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators when they were dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI.
Alas, the custom build turned into reality because the aftermarket outlet decided to bring it to life with the looks of a GX and the body of a Tacoma plus ultra-serious off-road chops. However, TMNA would never do it like this. Instead, they might use the larger Toyota Tundra for a simple rebadge featuring the current Lexus tough SUV design language.
That’s the whole idea behind this other virtual project - Jim, a virtual artist known as " jlord8 " on social media, loves messing around with all things CGI from the automotive realm, and he dreams of a Lexus truck that’s called TX 650 and has the face of the GX plastered on top of the Tundra body.
As it turns out, people liked both the color and the interesting CGI mashup. Someone even found its perfect customer base – folks running around between the ranch and the country club. Albeit, it would need an appropriate Lexus-style upgrade to the interior, too, along with a powerful powertrain setup. So, what do you think? Yay or nay for this unofficial, hypothetical design project? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Jim (@jlord8)
